summary: This is a SPEC-ONLY artifact (no code changes to server.py or any _.py module; no new MCP tool is implemented or registered). It closes the B276 gap list by defining: (1) a 5-kind event taxonomy (completion, failure, stale, usage, duplicate_runner) with an exact JSON payload schema per kind plus a shared envelope; (2) an opaque delta-cursor design so a caller can ask for 'what changed since cursor X' instead of re-diffing a full snapshot client-side; (3) an 'automatic loop, no manual polling' definition that is honest about what it does NOT provide -- it specifies Codex's OWN agent loop calling a proposed aiworkhub_completion_inbox_delta tool once per orchestration cycle using a cursor it persists itself, not a kernel-level push/webhook/inotify/daemon. No such tool is implemented here; server.py is unmodified. The spec explicitly keeps every process-launch and notification-delivery capability at the design stage and defers implementation, owner-channel wiring (email/Slack/desktop), and cursor-persistence-ownership to next-wave tasks that require additional infra/secrets decisions the owner has not yet made.

section_1_event_taxonomy.title: Owner-Notification Event Taxonomy (5 kinds, mandatory)
section_1_event_taxonomy.description: Every event the notification loop can emit is exactly one of these 5 kinds. Each kind's payload is derived from an EXISTING read-only data source already in server.py / completion_inbox.py; no new data collection code is specified.

completion.trigger_condition: task lifecycle_state transitions to 'review' (worker ran taskctl.py review, never done)

failure.derived_from: completion_inbox.build_completion_inbox()['latest_validation_facts'] where validation_status == 'FAIL' or blocker_reason is non-null
failure.trigger_condition: most recent recorded validation_status for a task is FAIL, or a blocker_reason string is present

stale.trigger_condition: task lifecycle_state == 'processing' with no artifact/validation activity for longer than stale_processing_hours

usage.derived_from: core.usage_report() (existing aiworkhub_task_usage_report tool) plus the B276 15-field launch log schema's usage_input_tokens/usage_output_tokens/cost_usd fields (spec-only in B276, still spec-only here -- no launch log file is created by this task)
usage.trigger_condition: a usage record exists for task_id/runner (recorded via taskctl.py usage, an already-existing command)

duplicate_runner.derived_from: core.collision_guard() (existing aiworkhub_task_collision_guard tool) for same-task_id double-claim, and completion_inbox's runner_mismatch_warnings (B275) for batch-token mismatch between a runner name and the task_id it claimed
duplicate_runner.trigger_condition: collision_guard reports 2 distinct runner values that both claim the same task_id, OR a runner_task_batch_mismatch entry is present

section_1_event_taxonomy.closes_gap: NO_ARTIFACT_BODY_READ is explicitly NOT closed by this taxonomy -- every payload above is metadata (task-card fields), never the body of a worker-produced JSON/JSONL artifact. This is stated as a remaining gap in section_1_remaining_gaps below, not silently dropped.

section_1_remaining_gaps_not_solved_by_t: NO_ARTIFACT_BODY_READ: still open -- this spec's event payloads are task-card metadata only, never artifact file contents.
NO_OWNER_DELIVERY_CHANNEL: still open -- no email/Slack/desktop-notify/log-tail target is designed or wired; see next_wave blockers.
NO_TRUE_PUSH: still open -- everything below is a caller-invoked read, not a kernel push/webhook/inotify/DB-trigger. See section_3.

section_2_payload_envelope_schema.title: Exact MCP Payload Envelope (shared by every event kind)
section_2_payload_envelope_schema.description: Every emitted event, regardless of kind, is wrapped in this exact envelope. event-kind-specific fields listed in section_1 live under 'payload'.

envelope_schema.event_id: string, deterministic sha1(task_id + event_kind + detected_at + cursor_token)[:16] -- NOT a random uuid, so the same underlying state always regenerates the same event_id (idempotent, dedup-safe if replayed)
envelope_schema.event_kind: string enum: completion | failure | stale | usage | duplicate_runner
envelope_schema.task_id: string, the affected task card id (or primary task_id for duplicate_runner)
envelope_schema.runner: string | null, the owning runner at detection time
envelope_schema.detected_at: string, ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of this read (NOT the underlying DB event time -- this is a read/derive timestamp, see section_3 honesty note)
envelope_schema.cursor_token: string, opaque monotonic token identifying this event's position in the ordered stream -- see section_2b
envelope_schema.payload: object, event-kind-specific fields exactly as enumerated in section_1.event_kinds.<kind>.payload_fields
envelope_schema.authority_flags: object, see section_4 -- always all-false, embedded per-event so a downstream consumer never has to trust a top-level-only flag block
envelope_schema.source_facet: string, which existing read-only facet/tool produced this event (e.g. 'completion_inbox.review_queue', 'core.collision_guard', 'core.usage_report')

section_2b_delta_cursor_mechanism.title: Delta Cursor Design (closes NO_DELTA_CURSOR)
section_2b_delta_cursor_mechanism.description: Closes the B276 gap where aiworkhub_completion_inbox returns the FULL snapshot every call with no way to ask for only what's new. This section is a DESIGN, not an implementation -- no cursor storage code or new tool is added to server.py in this task.
section_2b_delta_cursor_mechanism.cursor_token_format: base64( max(updated_at across all facets) + '|' + sorted(task_ids already emitted at that exact updated_at) ) -- the tie-break list handles same-timestamp bursts so no event at the boundary is silently dropped or double-counted
section_2b_delta_cursor_mechanism.cursor_ownership: CALLER-OWNED, not server-owned. The proposed aiworkhub_completion_inbox_delta(topic, since_cursor) tool stays a pure function of (live queue state, since_cursor) -- it persists nothing itself. Codex (or whatever orchestrator calls it) is responsible for storing the returned next_cursor and passing it back next call. This keeps the MCP server stateless and read-only, consistent with every other tool in server.py.
section_2b_delta_cursor_mechanism.proposed_tool_signature: aiworkhub_completion_inbox_delta(topic: str | None = None, since_cursor: str | None = None, limit: int = 200) -> dict[str, Any] -- NOT IMPLEMENTED by this task. Returns {events: [envelope, ...], next_cursor: str, counts: {by_kind...}, truncated: bool, authority_flags: {...}}
section_2b_delta_cursor_mechanism.ack_dedup_note: closes NO_ACK_OR_DEDUP_MARKER partially: because event_id is deterministic (section_2), a caller that stores the last N seen event_ids can dedup trivially without a server-side 'seen' flag. This still requires the CALLER to keep that set; the server records no per-consumer ack state (consistent with keeping the MCP tool read-only/stateless).

section_3_automatic_loop_definition_no_m.title: What 'without manual polling' means here (and what it does NOT mean)
section_3_automatic_loop_definition_no_m.honest_framing: This spec does NOT define a push/webhook/inotify/DB-trigger/message-queue. No such mechanism is implemented, and none is claimed to exist. 'Without manual polling' means: a human owner never has to run a shell command or open a file to check for new events -- instead, an ALREADY-RUNNING Codex orchestration agent calls one MCP tool (aiworkhub_completion_inbox_delta, proposed, not yet implemented) at the top of its own loop iteration, exactly the way it already calls taskctl.py auto-pickup / aiworkhub_supervisor_loop_status today. The polling is automatic-within-the-agent-loop, not manual-by-a-person. It remains, mechanically, a pull.
loop_steps: 1. Codex orchestration loop starts an iteration (already an existing pattern -- same cadence as its auto-pickup loop).
2. Codex calls aiworkhub_completion_inbox_delta(topic=<its topic scope>, since_cursor=<cursor it stored last iteration>) -- proposed tool, not implemented in this task.
3. Tool returns {events: [...], next_cursor}; Codex stores next_cursor for the following iteration (caller-owned cursor, section_2b).

4. Codex branches on event_kind: completion -> run its existing review checklist (aiworkhub_task_codex_handoff); failure -> create a repair task per the B276 completion_return_path step 6; stale -> flag for owner attention; usage -> append to its own cost ledger; duplicate_runner -> run aiworkhub_task_collision_guard for the details and pause auto-pickup for that task_id.

5. If Codex itself is not currently running (session ended), NOTHING fires -- there is no background process. This is the honest limit: automatic-within-a-running-loop, not automatic-when-nothing-is-running.
not_claimed: no cron/systemd-timer/daemon is specified or implied
no inotify/DB-trigger on task_queue_v1.sqlite is specified or implied
no owner-facing delivery channel (email/Slack/desktop notify) is specified as ready -- see next_wave

section_4_authority_flags.title: Authority Flags (ALL FALSE, embedded in every envelope per section_2)

neural_bridge_note: This spec introduces no learned decision authority and no regex/keyword cue router: event_kind classification is a fixed 1:1 mapping from an already-recorded task-card field state (lifecycle_state, validation_status, stale threshold, presence of a usage record, collision_guard output) to one of 5 taxonomy labels -- a deterministic support-boundary/evidence-extraction mapping over existing fields, not a routing or intelligence decision. If a future task teaches a controller to PRIORITIZE or SUMMARIZE these events (e.g. which failure to fix first), that becomes a neural curriculum target per neural_bridge_priority; this task only defines the deterministic event shape it would consume.
